content.text:
**Elon Musk's xAI announcements** (primarily the company's founding in 2023 and subsequent major updates) have evolved significantly, with recent developments in 2025–2026 focusing on mergers, reorganizations, ambitious space-based AI plans, and product advancements like Grok.[[1]](https://techcrunch.com/2026/02/11/xai-lays-out-interplanetary-ambitions-in-public-all-hands/)

### Original xAI Announcement (July 2023)
Elon Musk founded xAI in July 2023 as a new AI company aimed at "understanding the true nature of the universe." It was positioned as a competitor to OpenAI (which Musk co-founded but later criticized), with a focus on building "maximum truth-seeking AI" and avoiding what he saw as excessive political correctness in other models. The initial team included former members from DeepMind, OpenAI, Google Research, Microsoft Research, and Tesla. Grok, xAI's chatbot inspired by the Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy and JARVIS from Iron Man, was announced shortly after as its flagship product.[[2]](https://www.reuters.com/technology/musks-xai-launch-improved-version-chatbot-2024-03-29/)

### Key Subsequent Announcements and Developments
- **Grok Improvements (2024)**: xAI released Grok-1.5 in March 2024, with notable gains in coding and math performance. It was made available to early testers and X Premium+ users. Musk also open-sourced the original Grok-1 model around that time.[[2]](https://www.reuters.com/technology/musks-xai-launch-improved-version-chatbot-2024-03-29/)

- **Acquisition of X (2025)**: In March 2025, xAI acquired the social media platform X (formerly Twitter, which Musk owns) in a $33 billion all-stock deal. This valued the combined entity at over $100 billion and integrated Grok more deeply with X's real-time data.[[3]](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-03-28/musk-says-that-his-xai-startup-has-acquired-x-for-33-billion?srnd=homepage-americas)

- **Major Merger with SpaceX (February 2026)**: SpaceX acquired xAI, forming a vertically integrated company valued at $1.25 trillion. The deal combined AI (Grok), rockets, Starlink, direct-to-mobile comms, and X. Musk emphasized space-based data centers for cheaper AI compute, stating that within 2–3 years, space could offer the lowest-cost AI processing due to abundant solar power. This was tied to plans for self-sustaining lunar bases, Mars civilization, and broader universe expansion. The merged entity later rebranded elements toward "SpaceXAI" by mid-2026.[[4]](https://www.theverge.com/tech/872619/elon-musk-merges-spacex-with-xai-and-x)

- **Reorganization and Interplanetary Ambitions (February 2026)**: Following the merger and several co-founder departures (leaving about half the original team), Musk restructured xAI into focused teams: Grok (including voice), coding, Imagine (video/image generation), and Macrohard (AI for automating companies/corporate modeling). In a rare public all-hands video posted on X, he outlined building moon-based AI satellite factories, lunar mass drivers (electromagnetic catapults), and massive space data centers capturing solar energy—potentially scaling to terawatts or even galactic levels. He described it as "incredibly exciting" to see what such intelligence would think about. This preceded a major IPO.[[1]](https://techcrunch.com/2026/02/11/xai-lays-out-interplanetary-ambitions-in-public-all-hands/)

- **Other Projects**: Announcements included a massive 500-megawatt data center in Saudi Arabia (2025, in partnership with HUMAIN AI, powered by Nvidia chips) and rapid progress in image/video generation (e.g., outpacing some Google models). Musk has repeatedly highlighted "maximally truth-seeking" AI, humanoid robots as a massive future product, and using xAI to support Tesla, SpaceX, and broader scientific breakthroughs.[[5]](https://www.aol.com/articles/elon-musk-announces-massive-xai-172332381.html?guccounter=1)

These announcements reflect Musk's vision of tightly integrating AI with space infrastructure for unprecedented scale. For the latest details, check official posts on X from @elonmusk, @xai, or @SpaceX.
